99: The provisions in the following chapters and sections shall constitute and be designated as the "Code of Ordinances, City of Hiawassee, Georgia," and may be so cited. Such Code may also be cited as "Hiawassee City Code."
100:
In the construction of this Code and of all ordinances, the following definitions and rules of construction shall be observed, unless inconsistent with the manifest intent of city council or the context clearly requires otherwise:
Advice and consent. The term "advice and consent" of the city council means an affirmative vote of the majority of the entire council.
Bond. When a bond is required, an undertaking in writing shall be sufficient.
City. The term "the city" means the City of Hiawassee in the County of Towns and the State of Georgia, except as otherwise provided.
City council, the council. The terms "city council" and "the council" mean the city council of the City of Hiawassee, Georgia.
Code. The term "Code" means the Code of Ordinances, City of Hiawassee, Georgia, as designated in section 1-1.
Computation of time. Except as otherwise provided by time period computations specifically applying to other laws, when a period of time measured in days, weeks, months, years or other measurements of time except hours is prescribed for the exercise of any privilege or the discharge of any duty, the first day shall not be counted but the last day shall be counted; and, if the last day falls on Saturday or Sunday, the party having such privilege or duty shall have through the following Monday to exercise the privilege or to discharge the duty. When the last day prescribed for such action falls on a public and legal holiday as set forth in O.C.G.A. § 1-4-1, the party having the privilege or duty shall have through the next business day to exercise the privilege or to discharge the duty. When the period of time prescribed is less than seven days, intermediate Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays shall be excluded in the computation.
County, the county. The terms "county" and "the county" mean the County of Towns, State of Georgia.
Court. The term "court," unless otherwise indicated, means the Municipal Court of the City of Hiawassee, Georgia.
Day. The term "day" means a calendar day of 24 hours.
Delegation of authority. Whenever a provision appears requiring the head of a department of the city to do some act or make certain inspections, it is to be construed to authorize the head of the department to designate, delegate and authorize subordinates to perform the required act or make the required inspection unless the terms of the provision or section designate otherwise.
Gender. Words importing the masculine gender shall include the feminine and neuter.
Governing body. The term "governing body" means the mayor and city council of the City of Hiawassee, Georgia.
Joint authority. All words giving joint authority to three or more persons or officers shall be construed as giving such authority to a majority of such persons or officers, except when such words are used to grant authority to the mayor and council.
Mayor. The term "mayor" means the mayor of the City of Hiawassee, Georgia.
Month. The term "month" means a calendar month.
Names of officers and departments. The name or title of any officer or department shall be read as though the words "of the City of Hiawassee" were added to such name or title.
Nontechnical and technical words. Words and phrases shall be construed according to the common and approved usage of the language, but technical words and phrases and such others as may have acquired a peculiar and appropriate meaning in law shall be construed and understood according to such meaning.
Number. Words used in the singular include the plural, and the plural includes the singular number.
Oath. The term "oath" shall be construed to include an affirmation in all cases in which, by law, an affirmation may be substituted for an oath; and in such cases, the terms "swear" and "sworn" shall be equivalent to the terms "affirm" and "affirmed."
O.C.G.A. The abbreviation "O.C.G.A." means the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, as amended.
Or, and. The term "or" may be read "and," and the term "and" may be read "or," as the sense requires.
Owner. The term "owner," applied to a building or land, includes any part owner, joint owner, tenant in common, joint tenant or tenant by the entirety, of the whole or a part of such building or land.
Penal ordinances. The rules of construction and definitions of words as contained in the penal code of the state, unless otherwise indicated and insofar as they can be made applicable, are adopted as governing the penal ordinances of the city.
Person. The term "person" includes a corporation, firm, partnership, association, organization, nonprofit organization and any other group acting as a unit, as well as an individual.
Personal property. The term "personal property" includes every species of property except real property.
Preceding, following. The terms "preceding" and "following" mean next before and next after, respectively.
Premises. Whenever the term "premises" is used, it means place or places.
Property. The term "property" includes real and personal property.
Public place. The term "public place" means any park, cemetery, schoolyard or open space adjacent thereto, or any area available and/or accessible to the public, regardless of whether privately or publicly owned.
Real property. The term "real property" includes lands, tenements and hereditaments.
Reasonable time or notice. Reasonable time or notice, unless indicated otherwise or a different meaning is required by law, shall be deemed to mean only such time as may be necessary for the prompt performance of the act required.
Residence. The term "residence" shall be construed to mean the place adopted by a person as his place of habitation, and to which, whenever he is absent, he has the intention of returning. When a person eats at one place and sleeps at another, the place where such person sleeps shall be deemed his residence.
Seal. The term "seal" means the city seal.
Shall, may. The term "shall" is mandatory; the term "may" is permissive.
Sheriff. The term "sheriff" means the sheriff of Towns County, Georgia.
Sidewalk. The term "sidewalk" means any portion of a street between the curbline and the adjacent property line, intended for the use of pedestrians, but shall not include any unimproved areas between the curbline and improved walkways.
Signature, subscription. The terms "signature" and "subscription" include a mark when the person cannot write.
State, the state. The terms "state" and "the state" mean the State of Georgia.
Street. The term "street" means and includes any public way, road, highway, street, avenue, boulevard, parkway, alley, lane, viaduct, bridge and their approaches within the city and includes all parts thereof constituting the designated right-of-way.
Tenant, occupant. The terms "tenant" and "occupant," applied to a building or land, include any person who occupies the whole or a part of such building or land, whether alone or with others.
Tense. Words used in the past or present tense include the future as well as the past and present.
Week. The term "week" means a calendar week of seven days.
Written, in writing. The terms "written" and "in writing" include printing and any other mode of representing words and letters.
Year. The term "year" means a calendar year.
101: The catchlines of sections in this Code printed in boldface type, italics or otherwise are intended as mere catchwords to indicate the contents of the sections, and shall not be deemed or taken to be titles of such sections, nor as any part of the section, nor, unless expressly so provided, shall they be so deemed when any of such sections, including the catchlines, are amended or reenacted. The history notes appearing in parentheses after each section and the references and editor's notes scattered throughout this Code are for the benefit of the user of this Code and shall have no legal effect.
102: It is declared to be the intention of the city council that the sections, paragraphs, sentences, clauses and phrases of this Code are severable; and if any phrase, clause, sentence, paragraph or section of this Code shall be declared or adjudged to be invalid or unconstitutional, by the valid judgment or decree of any court of competent jurisdiction, such declaration or adjudication shall not affect any of the remaining phrases, clauses, sentences, paragraphs and sections of this Code since they would have been enacted by the council without the incorporation in this Code of any such invalid or unconstitutional phrase, clause, sentence, paragraph or section.
103:
(a) The repeal of an ordinance, or its expiration by virtue of any provision contained in the ordinance, shall not affect any right accrued or any offense committed, any penalty or punishment incurred or any proceeding commenced before the repeal took effect or the ordinance expired.
(b) When an ordinance that repealed another shall itself be repealed, the previous ordinance shall not be revived without express words to that effect.
(c) An ordinance which is in conflict in its entirety with a subsequent ordinance shall be deemed to be repealed in its entirety, even if no specific repealer is stated. If an ordinance is only partially in conflict with a subsequent ordinance, only the portion of the previous ordinance in conflict with the subsequent ordinance shall be deemed to have been repealed, even if a specific repealer is not stated.
104:
In a provision involving two or more items, conditions, provisions or events, which items, conditions, provisions or events are connected by the conjunction "and," "or" or "either . . . or," the conjunction shall be interpreted as follows, except that in appropriate cases, the terms "or" and "and" are interchangeable:
(1) "And" indicates that all the connected terms, conditions, provisions or events apply.
(2) "Or" indicates that the connected terms, conditions, provisions or events apply singly or in any combination.
(3) "Either . . . or" indicates that the connected terms, conditions, provisions or events apply singly but not in combination.
105: Where any provision of this Code, or state statutes or regulations, impose greater restrictions upon the subject matter than any general provisions imposed by this Code or the mandatory provisions of state statute or regulations, the provision imposing the greater restriction or regulation shall be applicable.
106:
(a) Nothing in this Code or the ordinance adopting this Code shall be construed to repeal or otherwise affect the validity of any of the following:
(1) Any offense or act committed or done or any penalty or forfeiture incurred or any contract or right established or accruing before the effective date of this Code.
(2) Any ordinance or resolution promising or guaranteeing the payment of money for the city or authorizing the issuance of any bonds of the city or any evidence of the city's indebtedness.
(3) Any contract or obligation assumed by the city.
(4) Any ordinance fixing the salary of any city officer or employee.
(5) Any right or franchise granted by the city.
(6) Any ordinance dedicating, naming, establishing, locating, relocating, opening, widening, paving, etc., any street or public way in the city.
(7) Any appropriation ordinance.
(8) Any ordinance which, by its own terms, is effective for a stated or limited term.
(9) Any ordinance providing for local improvements and assessing taxes for such improvements.
(10) Any zoning ordinance.
(11) Any ordinance dedicating or accepting any subdivision plat.
(12) Any ordinance describing or altering the boundaries of the city.
(13) The administrative ordinances or resolutions of the city not in conflict or inconsistent with the provisions of this Code.
(14) Any ordinance levying or imposing taxes not included in this Code.
(15) Any ordinance establishing or prescribing street grades in the city.
(b) No ordinance in subsection (a) of this section shall be construed to revive any ordinance or part thereof that has been repealed by a subsequent ordinance which is repealed by this chapter. All ordinances in subsection (a) of this section are recognized as continuing in full force and effect to the same extent as if set out at length in this Code.
107: The provisions appearing in this Code, so far as they are the same as ordinances adopted prior to this Code and included in such Code, shall be considered as continuations thereof and not as new enactments.
108:
(a) All ordinances passed subsequent to this Code that amend, repeal or in any way affect this Code may be numbered in accordance with the numbering system of this Code and printed for inclusion in this Code. In the case of repealed chapters, sections and subsections or any part thereof, by subsequent ordinances, such repealed portions may be excluded from this Code by their omission from reprinted pages. The subsequent ordinances as numbered and printed or omitted, in the case of repeal, shall be prima facie evidence of such subsequent ordinances until such time that this Code and subsequent ordinances numbered or omitted are readopted as a new code by the city council.
(b) Amendments to any of the provisions of this Code may be made by amending such provisions by specific reference to the section number of this Code.
(c) If a new section not heretofore existing in this Code is to be added, the following language may be used: "That The Code of the City of Hiawassee, Georgia, is hereby amended by adding a section, article or chapter to be numbered _____, which section, article or chapter reads as follows:…." The new section, article or chapter may then be set out in full as desired.
(d) All sections, articles, chapters or provisions desired to be repealed should be specifically repealed by section, article or chapter number, as the case may be.
109:
(a) By contract or by city personnel, supplements to this Code shall be prepared at least on an annual basis. A supplement to this Code shall include all substantive, permanent and general parts of ordinances passed by the city council during the period covered by the supplement and all changes made thereby in this Code. The pages of a supplement shall be so numbered that they will fit properly into this Code and will, where necessary, replace pages that have become obsolete or partially obsolete; and the new pages shall be so prepared that, when they have been inserted, this Code will be current through the date of the adoption of the latest ordinance included in the supplement.
(b) In preparing a supplement to this Code, all portions of this Code that have been repealed shall be excluded from this Code by their omission thereof from reprinted pages.
(c) When preparing a supplement to this Code, the codifier (meaning the person authorized to prepare the supplement) may make formal, nonsubstantive changes in ordinances and parts of ordinances included in the supplement, insofar as it is necessary to do so to embody them into a unified code. For example, the codifier may:
(1) Organize the ordinance material into appropriate subdivisions.
(2) Provide appropriate catchlines, headings and titles for sections and other subdivisions of this Code printed in the supplement, and make changes in such catchlines, headings and titles.
(3) Assign appropriate numbers to sections and other subdivisions to be inserted in this Code and, where necessary to accommodate new material, change existing section or other subdivision numbers.
(4) Change the words "this ordinance" or words of the same meaning to "this chapter," "this article," or "this section," as the case may be, or to "sections _____ to _____" (inserting section numbers to indicate the sections of this Code that embody the substantive sections of the ordinance incorporated into this Code).
(5) Make other nonsubstantive changes necessary to preserve the original meanings of ordinance sections inserted into this Code; but in no case shall the codifier make any change in the meaning or effect of ordinance material included in the supplement or already embodied in this Code.
110: It shall be unlawful for any person in the city to change or amend by additions or deletions any part or portion of this Code, or to insert or delete pages, or portions of pages, or to alter or tamper with such Code in any manner whatsoever which will cause the law of the city to be misrepresented thereby, unless so authorized by ordinance or resolution or other official act of the city council. Any person violating this section shall be punished as provided in section 1-13.
111:
(a) In this section "violation of this Code" or "violation of any such provision of this Code or any such ordinance" means any of the following:
(1) Doing an act that is prohibited or made or declared unlawful, an offense, a violation or a misdemeanor by ordinance, by statute adopted by reference in this Code, by state rule or regulation adopted by reference in this Code, or by rule or regulation authorized by ordinance.
(2) Failure to perform an act that is required to be performed by ordinance, by statute adopted by reference in this Code, by state rule or regulation adopted by reference in this Code or by rule or regulation authorized by ordinance.
(3) Failure to perform an act if the failure is prohibited or is made or declared unlawful, an offense, a violation or a misdemeanor by ordinance, by statute adopted by reference in this Code, by state rule or regulation adopted by reference in this Code or by rule or regulation authorized by ordinance.
(b) In this section "violation of this Code" or "violation of any such provision of this Code or any such ordinance" does not include the failure of a city officer or city employee to perform an official duty unless it is specifically provided that the failure to perform the duty is to be punished as provided in this section.
(c) Unless another penalty is otherwise specified, whenever in this Code or in any ordinance of the city any act is prohibited or is made or declared to be unlawful or an offense, or whenever in this Code or any ordinance the doing of any act is required and the failure to do such act is declared to be unlawful, and no specific penalty is provided, and unless otherwise provided by state law, the violation of any such provision of this Code or any such ordinance shall be punished by a fine not to exceed $1,000.00 and imprisonment not exceeding six months, or both such fine and imprisonment, or the court may fix punishment by fine, imprisonment, or alternative sentencing as now or hereafter provided by state law or local ordinance. Each day any violation of this Code or of any ordinance shall continue shall constitute a separate offense.
(d) Violations of this Code may be abated by injunctive or other equitable relief. The imposition of a penalty does not prevent injunctive relief.
(e) The infliction of a penalty under the provisions of this section shall not prevent the revocation of any permit or license or the taking of other punitive or remedial action where called for or permitted under the provisions of the city's Charter or Code.
State Law reference— Maximum penalty for ordinance violation, O.C.G.A. § 36-35-6(a)(2).

114: The fiscal year for the city shall run from July 1 through June 30 of each year.
115: The city shall maintain a consolidated fee schedule for permits, licenses and other city fees, charges and costs, including those for utility services. Unless otherwise indicated, the amount of any fees, charges and costs imposed by the city, including, but not limited to, those set forth in the city's consolidated fee schedule, shall be established from time to time by action of the city council as it deems necessary. A copy of the consolidated fee schedule shall be on file in the office of the city clerk and be made available for public examination during normal working hours.
116: A police standard operating procedure manual may be adopted from time to time by action of the city council. Any such manual will be adopted only after the council receives input and suggestions from the chief of police and any other city departments or officials the council deems appropriate. Once adopted, the city chief of police is fully empowered and authorized to enforce all of the provisions and requirements therein. A copy of this manual shall be on file in the office of the city clerk and be made available for public examination during normal business hours.
117: Unless otherwise addressed in this Code or the city Charter, all city personnel policy shall be as set out in the city's personnel policy manual, which may be amended from time to time by action of the city council, and which shall be made available for examination and copying in the office of the city clerk during normal business hours.
120:
In order to guide and accomplish a coordinated and harmonious development of the municipality which will, in accordance with existing and future needs, and in accordance with the city's enacted comprehensive land-disturbing activities and commercial development standards, specifications, and rules and regulations which will assist in protecting the environment and in meeting the needs of state and federal officials, the city planning committee is created and established.
(Ord. No. 0113, 2-5-2008)
121:
The planning committee shall consist of five members, appointed as follows:
(1) Two city councilmembers designated by resolution of the city council; and
(2) Three residents of the city designated by resolution of the city council.
Each member of the city planning committee shall serve at the pleasure of the city council and until their successor is appointed.
(Ord. No. 0102, § 6, 6-5-2007; Ord. No. 0113, § 1, 2-5-2008)
122:
The planning committee shall elect its chairman and vice-chairman from among its members. Their terms shall be two years with eligibility for re-election. The committee shall make its own rules of procedure and, subject to approval of city council, determine its time of meeting. All meetings of the planning committee at which official action is taken shall be open to the public, and all records of the planning committee shall be a public record. All members shall serve without compensation but may be reimbursed for actual expenses incurred in connection with their official duties.
(Ord. No. 0113, § 1, 2-5-2008)
124:
(a) The planning committee shall develop rules and regulations, forms and applications, as necessary and appropriate for the administration of and implementation of the 2007 comprehensive planning ordinance, the 2017 planning-development ordinance and the Mountain Protection Act.
(b) The planning committee shall serve in an advisory capacity to the mayor, or appointed designee, and the city council for the administration of the 2007 comprehensive planning ordinance, the 2017 planning-development ordinance and the Mountain Protection Act.
(Ord. No. 0113, § 2, 2-5-2008)
125:
(a) The city planning commission, along with the mayor or appointed designee, city staff, the city engineers and/or other city's designated representative, are delegated the authority to enter upon the subject property of any applicant over which the city has jurisdiction under the 2007 comprehensive planning ordinance, the 2017 planning-development ordinance and under the Mountain Protection Act for the purposes of verifying the information contained within any application and to determine whether there has been compliance during land-disturbing activity and/or construction or erection of improvements, with either ordinance or with the plans submitted as part of any application to the committee.
(b) In the event of a failure to comply with either ordinance or plans submitted, upon the request of the chairman of the planning committee, the mayor or appointed designee is hereby delegated the authority to issue a stop-work order. Said stop-work order shall be provided by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the applicant and the owner of the property as disclosed on the application, and such order shall specify the act of noncompliance, and what acts must be taken by the owner to be in compliance with this ordinance or such plans.
(c) Said action and further proceedings shall be as specified with the 2007 comprehensive planning ordinance, the 2017 planning-development ordinance and the Mountain Protection Act; and the chairman and the committee and the mayor or appointed designee shall be empowered to act in accordance therewith.
(Ord. No. 0113, § 3, 2-5-2008)
126:
The board of ethics members shall be appointed, removed, qualified and serve as set out in this section.
(1) The board of ethics of the city shall consist of three residents of the city, one appointed by the mayor, one appointed by the city council, and the third appointed by the mayor and approved by a majority of the city council.
(2) All members of the board of ethics shall be residents of the city for at least one year immediately preceding the date of taking office and shall remain a resident while serving on the board.
(3) All members of the board of ethics shall serve a two-year term.
(4) No person shall serve as a member of the board of ethics if the person has, or has had, within the preceding one-year period, any interest in any contract or contracting opportunity with the city or has been employed by the city.
(5) Members of the board of ethics with any permit, building or planning application pending before the city, or any pending or potential litigation against the city or any city official charged in the complaint shall be disqualified from serving on the board of ethics for that complaint. An alternate member of the board of ethics shall be selected in the same manner as the disqualified individual.
(6) The members of the board of ethics shall serve without compensation. The city council shall provide meeting space for the board of ethics and, subject to budgetary procedures and requirements of the city, such supplies and equipment as may be reasonably necessary for the board to perform its duties and responsibilities.
(7) No person shall serve on the board of ethics who has been convicted of a felony involving moral turpitude in this state or any other state, unless such person's civil rights have been restored and at least ten years have elapsed from the date of the completion of the sentence without a subsequent conviction of another felony involving moral turpitude.
(8) No person shall serve on the board of ethics who is less than 21 years of age, who holds a public elective office, who is physically or mentally unable to discharge the duties of a member of the board of ethics, or who is not qualified to be a registered voter in the city.
(9) Upon appointment, members of the board of ethics shall sign an affidavit attesting to their qualification to serve as a member of the board of ethics.
(10) Members of the board of ethics may be removed by majority vote of the city governing authority for cause, including, but not limited to, failure to maintain any requirement for qualification to serve on the board of ethics.
(Ord. of 2-7-2017(3), § 1(6))
127:
There is hereby created and established a city tree board, which shall consist of members of city residents and staff appointed by the city council.
(Ord. No. 2018-05-02, § 1, 5-1-2018)
128:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this subsection, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Street trees means trees and other woody vegetation on land lying between property lines on either side of all streets, avenues, or ways within the city.
(Ord. No. 2018-05-02, intro., 5-1-2018)
129:
Members of the board shall serve without compensation.
(Ord. No. 2018-05-02, § 2, 5-1-2018)
130:
It shall be the responsibility of the board to study, investigate, counsel, and develop and/or update annually, and administer a written plan for the care, conservation, pruning, planting, replanting, removal or disposition of trees, along streets and in other public areas. The board shall consider, investigate, make findings, report and recommend to the city council upon any special matter of question coming within the scope of its work.
(Ord. No. 2018-05-02, § 3, 5-1-2018)
131:
The board shall make its own rules and regulations and operate meetings under Robert's Rules of Order. A majority of the members shall be a quorum for the transaction of business.
(Ord. No. 2018-05-02, § 4, 5-1-2018)
134: Pursuant to Charter section 5.10, all primaries and elections shall be held and conducted in accordance with the Georgia Municipal Election Code, O.C.G.A. § 21-2-1 et seq.
135: The polling place within the city shall be the elections board or some other location as determined by the city council from time to time. The city clerk, as required by O.C.G.A. § 21-2-265, shall take such steps as may be necessary to notify voters of any polling place change.
136: The city clerk is hereby appointed as the city election superintendent and shall provide the necessary materials for conducting any city election. If the mayor and city council so deem appropriate, the city may contract with the county or another third party to conduct any such election on the city's behalf.
139:
The city personnel policy management system has been established by the city council as the city personnel policies governing personnel policy and procedure within the city, and it may be amended or modified or added to/from time to time by resolution of the council. A copy of these policies and procedures has been made available to all city employees and is on file in the office of the city clerk for public examination and review during normal business hours.
(Ord. No. 2019-07-01, § 1, 7-9-2019)
142:
This article shall be known as the "City of Hiawassee Identity Theft Prevention Ordinance".
(Ord. No. 0130, § 1, 7-7-2009)
143:
The purpose of the ordinance is to comply with 16 CFR § 681.2, in order to detect, prevent and mitigate identity theft by identifying and detecting identity theft red flags and by responding to such red flags in a manner that will prevent identity theft.
(Ord. No. 0130, § 2, 7-7-2009)
144:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Covered account means a water or sewer utility account established with the city that involves or is designed to permit multiple payments or transactions, and any other account that the city offers or maintains for which there is a reasonably foreseeable risk to customers or to the city from identity theft including financial, operational, compliance, reputation, or litigation risks.
Credit means the right granted by the city to defer payment for services to customers.
Creditor means any person who regularly arranges for the extension, renewal, or continuation of credit; or any assignee of an original creditor who participates in the decision to extend, renew, or continue credit.
Customer means a person that has a covered account established with the city.
Identity theft means a fraud committed or attempted using identifying information of another person without authority.
Personal identifying information means a person's credit card account information, debit card information, bank account information, employment information numbers, driver's license information, any identifying number assigned by state or local government, and, for a natural person, includes their social security number, mother's birth name, and date of birth.
Red flag means a pattern, practice, or specific activity that indicates the possible existence of identity theft.
Service provider means a person that provides a service.
(Ord. No. 0130, § 3, 7-7-2009)
145:
(a) The city is a creditor pursuant to 16 CFR § 681.2, due to its provision or maintenance of covered accounts for which payments for services are made in arrears.
(b) Covered accounts offered to customers for the provision of city services include water and sewer accounts.
(c) There has been no previous experience with identity theft related to covered accounts experienced by the city.
(d) The processes of opening a new covered count, restoring an existing covered account, making payments on such accounts, and allowing third persons to make payment on an account on behalf of a customer have been identified as potential processes in which identity theft could occur.
(e) The city limits access to personal identifying information to those employees responsible for or otherwise involved in opening or restoring covered accounts or accepting payment for use of covered accounts. Information provided to such employees is entered directly into the city's computer system and is not otherwise recorded.
(f) The city determines that there is a low risk of identity theft occurring in the following ways:
(1) Use by an applicant of another person's personal identifying information to establish a new covered account;
(2) Use of a previous customer's personal identifying information by another person in an effort to have service restored in the previous customer's name;
(3) Use of another person's credit card, bank account, or other method of payment by a customer to pay such customer's covered account;
(4) Use by a customer desiring to restore such customer's covered account of another person's credit card, bank account, or other method of payment.
(Ord. No. 0130, § 4, 7-7-2009)
147:
(a) Access to customer accounts shall be password protected and shall be limited to authorized city personnel.
(b) Such password shall be changed by the mayor or appointed designee, by a contractor of information technology on direction of the mayor, or by the billing department clerk on a regular basis.
(c) Such password shall be at least eight characters in length and shall contain letters, numbers and symbols as determined appropriate by the mayor or appointed designee, after consultation with the contractor of information technology.
(d) Any unauthorized access to or other breach of customer accounts is to be reported immediately to the mayor or appointed designee, the city attorney, and the chief of police and the password changed immediately.
(e) Personal identifying information included in customer accounts is considered confidential and any request or demand for such information shall be immediately forwarded to the mayor or appointed designee and the city attorney.
(Ord. No. 0130, § 6, 7-7-2009)
148:
(a) In the event that credit card payments are made over the Internet or are processed through a third party service provider, such third party service provider shall certify that it has an adequate identity theft prevention program in place that is applicable to such payments.
(b) All credit card payments made over the telephone or the city's website shall be entered directly into the customer's account information in the computer database.
(c) Account statements and receipts for covered accounts shall include only the last four digits of the credit or debit card or the bank account used for payment of the covered account.
(Ord. No. 0130, § 7, 7-7-2009)
152:
(a) The mayor or appointed designee, with the assistance of the city attorney, is responsible for the oversight of the program and for program implementation. The mayor or appointed designee is responsible for reviewing reports prepared by staff regarding compliance with red flag requirements and with recommending material changes to the program, as necessary in the opinion of the mayor or appointed designee, to address changing identity theft risks and to identify new or discontinued types of covered accounts. Any recommended material changes to the program shall be submitted to the city council for consideration by the council.
(b) The mayor or appointed designee will report to the city council at least annually, on compliance with the red flag requirements. The report will address material matters related to the program and evaluate issues such as:
(1) The effectiveness of the policies and procedures of the city in addressing the risk of identity theft in connection with the opening of covered accounts and existing covered accounts;
(2) Service provider arrangements;
(3) Significant incidents involving identity theft and management's response; and
(4) Recommendations for material changes to the program.
(c) The mayor or appointed designee and the city attorney are jointly responsible for providing training to all employees responsible for or involved in opening a new covered account, restoring an existing covered account or accepting payment for a covered account with respect to the implementation and requirements of the identity theft prevention program. The mayor or appointed designee shall exercise his discretion in determining the amount and substance of training necessary.

The purpose of the rules is to foster an atmosphere of civil and courteous discourse, even and especially when discussing contentious topics, at all meetings held by the City of Hiawassee. These rules are also intended to create an environment in which the city's elected officials can conduct the public's business in a reasonably timely manner and without undue disruption or interruptions.
(1) Except as specified below, comment will be during the public comment item on the work session agenda. Generally, public comment will be limited to 30 minutes but may be extended upon majority vote of the city council. Any person not a member of city council who desires to address the city council shall first sign in at the beginning of the work session or meeting, giving his or her address and the subject they wish to speak about. Three minutes will be allowed for each person to speak. Grievances with individual employees may not be discussed. As you are selected to speak, you will be acknowledged by the presiding officer, and shall state your name and address in an audible tone of voice for the record. (Public comment may be allowed at regular voting meetings upon request by the mayor or presiding officer and approval of a majority of city council).
(2) Each speaker will direct his or her comments to the mayor or presiding officer and not to any other individual present. While speakers may pose questions, they should not expect an immediate response as city officials will normally take time to frame a response that can be provided at a later time.
(3) Each speaker will refrain from personal attacks, foul or abusive language, and will maintain a civil and courteous manner and tone.
(4) During consideration of agenda items, members of the public may ask questions or make comments, limited to no more than one minute. The mayor or presiding officer may limit questions or comment to five speakers on each agenda item; provided however, that city council by majority vote may allow additional speakers, specifying the number of additional speakers in the motion. At the discretion of the mayor and council, the limits set forth in this paragraph may be suspended by majority vote on particular agenda items.
(5) In instances in which the number of speakers or the time is limited, residents and persons owning property within the city limits of the city will be allowed to speak first. If all such persons have spoken and time remains, others will be permitted to speak. Those wishing to address the mayor and council that cannot do so due to time restrictions are encouraged to submit written comments.
(6) Members of the audience will respect the rights of others and will not create noise or other disturbances that will disrupt the meeting.
(7) Disruption of the meeting by members of the audience will not be tolerated. If, after a warning from the presiding officer, any person continues to disrupt the meeting by his or her words or actions, the presiding officer may request that person to leave the room, and then seek assistance from law enforcement officials to have the person removed from the meeting.
(8) Any person who disrupts, interrupts or interferes with a public meeting two or more times within a 12-month period will not be allowed to address the mayor and council in a public meeting until 30 days have lapsed from the second or subsequent offense. Such persons may still submit written comments.
(Ord. No. 2024-07-01, § 1, 8-6-2024)

The following procedures shall be followed for the removal of an officer by the city council for any of the causes specified in subsection 5.15(a) of the Charter:
(1) The city council shall designate the municipal court judge as the hearing officer to preside over the hearing of the allegations as specified in the notice required by subsection 5.15(b) of the Charter. If the municipal court judge cannot or will not serve for any reason, city council shall appoint a hearing officer who shall be a competent attorney at law in good standing in his or her profession with at least seven years' experience in the practice of law. Said hearing officer shall be paid the same hourly rate as that received by the city attorney.
(2) Recognizing that the city attorney has a conflict of interest in seeking removal of an elected official, the city shall be represented by a special city attorney retained by the city council for the purposes of this hearing.
(3) The following hearing procedures shall apply:
a. The hearing officer may issue subpoenas for witnesses or documents, enforceable as provided by law.
b. The burden of proving the allegations specified in the notice shall be on the person, persons or entity bringing the allegations. The burden of proof shall be by the preponderance of the evidence.
c. The hearing officer may apply the rules of evidence as applied in civil nonjury matters but shall, when necessary to ascertain facts not reasonably susceptible of proof under such rules, allow evidence not otherwise admissible thereunder if it is of a type commonly relied upon by reasonably prudent persons in the conduct of their affairs or if it consists of documents relied upon by the city in the normal course of its business.
d. Where practicable, a copy of each exhibit to be identified or tendered at the hearing shall be furnished to the hearing officer and the other parties at least three days before the hearing unless otherwise directed by the hearing officer.
e. The hearing officer shall give effect to statutory presumptions and the rules of privilege recognized by law.
f. Whenever any oral testimony sought to be admitted is excluded by the hearing officer, the proponent of the testimony may make an offer of proof by means of a brief statement on the record describing the excluded testimony. Whenever any documentary or physical evidence or written testimony sought to be admitted is excluded, it shall remain a part of the record as an offer of proof.
g. The parties shall be allowed full and thorough cross examination of any witnesses.
h. Evidentiary hearings either shall have their audio recorded by electronic means or be reported verbatim. Upon written request, a copy of the record of any oral proceeding shall be furnished to any party at the requesting party's expense.
(4) Within 15 days after the completion of the hearing, the city council shall make a written decision with findings and conclusions.
(5) If the city council votes to remove the officer, the officer may appeal the decision as allowed by the Charter and by law.
(Ord. No. 2023-11-01, § 1, 1-9-2024)

(a) No city official shall use such position to secure special privileges or exemptions for himself or others, or to secure confidential information for any purpose other than official duties on behalf of the city.

(1) This prohibition shall not be applicable to the professional activities of the city attorney in his work as an independent contractor and legal advisor on behalf of the city.

Manufacturer means any maker and/or producer that bottles, cans, or otherwise fills beverage containers for sale to distributors dealers or consumers any alcoholic beverage. The term also means:
(1) In the case of distilled spirits, any person engaged in distilling, rectifying, or blending any distilled spirits; provided, however, that a vintner that blends wine with distilled spirits to produce a fortified wine shall not be considered a manufacturer of distilled spirits;
(2) In the case of malt beverages and/or beer, any brewer; and
(3) In the case of wine and fortified wine, any vintner.
Manager means the employee who does or will actually manage or operate the premises (as defined herein) on a day-to-day basis and/or the employee who will be present for an entire event of a licensee/permit holder and who is at least 21 years of age.
Method of measuring. Unless otherwise provided by the Georgia Alcoholic Beverage Code, all measurements to determine distances required for the issuance of alcoholic beverage licenses shall be measured by the most direct route of travel on the ground and shall be measured in the following manner:
(1) In a straight line from the front door of the structure from which alcoholic beverages are sold or offered for sale;
(2) To the front door of the building of a church or government-owned treatment center or to the nearest property line of the real property being used for school or educational purposes.
Microbrewery means any brewery designed to accommodate the processing of fewer than 5,000 barrels of beer or ale within any consecutive 12-month period.
Mobile food vendor means a mobile seller of food that is lawfully located in a public place within the town square and sells prepared food for consumption by the public where the food is prepared by one or more food trucks or similar mobile kitchen(s).
Nonprofit organization means an entity which is exempt from federal income tax pursuant to the provisions of 26 U.S.C. §§ 501(c), 501(d), 501(e).
Outdoor dining area means a space/area in which a licensee serves food and beverages as part of the operation of the licensed premises that is outside of the enclosed building structure and is open to the air and weather. Said term shall include, but in no way be limited to, a sidewalk café or patio. An outdoor dining area must be located immediately adjacent to the licensed enclosed restaurant.
Package means a bottle, can, keg, barrel, box or other original consumer container.
Performance facility means a facility where the principal objective or business is the presentation of live music, mainline dramatic arts, plays, theatre productions, stand-up comedy, and/or similar ticketed events, except that no performance facility may feature, show, allow, promote, or advertise adult entertainment as defined and regulated in this Code, and by state law.
Person or entity means any individual, firm, partnership, cooperative, nonprofit membership corporation, joint venture, association, company, corporation, limited liability company, agency, syndicate, estate, trust, business trust, receiver, fiduciary, sole proprietorship, or other group or combination acting as a unit, whether such entity operates for profit or nonprofit.
Premises means the entire building, including patios, porches and decks. In some instances, where indicated, premises may also include the entrance area, parking lot and the entire lot or parcel wherein the licensed establishment is located.
Registered agent means a resident of the county designated who is named or designated by a corporation or company to receive official documents for the company and who is at least 21 years of age.
Retail consumption dealer means any person who sells alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises, at retail, only to consumers and not for resale.
Retail package dealer means any person or store for the retail package sale of beer, malt beverages or wine, or any combination thereof, by unbroken packages in sealed containers to consumers at retail only and not for resale.
Retail package store means a retail package store is any business establishment that sells unbroken alcoholic beverages, malt beverages, wine and distilled spirits packages, only at retail to consumers. Distilled spirits may be sold by the package upon passage of voter referendum.
School building means state, county, city, or church school building. Said term shall include only those structures in which instruction is offered.
Section means a division of this chapter and/or ordinance.
Single serving generally means 12 ounces of beer or malt beverage or five ounces of wine or one and one-half ounces of distilled spirits; however, in this section, single servings of beer or malt beverage shall include a container of up to 34 ounces in a single serving package and for wine up to nine ounces in a single serving package and for distilled spirits up to three ounces in a single serving package.
Sports club means an association or corporation organized and existing under the laws of the state, organized and operated primarily to provide a location for the patrons thereof to engage in sporting events.
Taproom means room or establishment operated by a licensed brewery where beer is served by the drink.
Town square means property of the city, towns county tax parcel ID H002153 located on Main Street, between River Street, Berrong Street and Bell Street in downtown Hiawassee.
Wholesaler or wholesale dealer means an entity that sells alcoholic beverages to other wholesale dealers, retail package dealers, retail package stores, or retail consumption dealers.
Wine means any alcoholic beverage containing not more than 24 percent alcohol made from fruits, berries, or grapes by natural fermentation. Wine includes, but is not limited to, all sparkling wines, champagnes, combinations of such beverages, vermouths, special natural wines, rectified wines, and like products.

195:
(a) City licensees and permit holders are required to be familiar with and to abide by all applicable state and city regulations and laws.
(b) No alcoholic beverages shall be manufactured, distributed, or sold in the city, except pursuant to this chapter.
(c) Only those alcoholic beverage licenses and permits enumerated in section 4-5 may be issued under this chapter.
(d) In determining whether any license or permit applied for under this chapter shall be granted, in addition to all other provisions of this chapter, the following shall be considered by the city in the public interest and welfare:
(1) The applicant's financial capability to conduct business;
(2) Whether, within the past five years, an applicant has violated any law or regulation relating to any alcoholic beverage business for which the applicant may have previously held a license or permit or in which the applicant may have had an ownership interest;
(3) Any manner in which the applicant conducted any alcoholic beverage business for which the applicant may have previously held a license or permit or in which the applicant may have had an ownership interest;
(4) The extent of the financial interest of the applicant or any member of his or her family in any wholesale alcoholic beverage business, in that no person or family member who has any financial interest in any wholesale alcoholic beverage business in this or any other state or country shall also have any financial interest in any retail alcoholic beverage business, and no financial aid or assistance to any licensee/permit holder under this chapter; from any wholesaler, distributor, or manufacturer of alcoholic beverages shall be permitted;
(5) No city employee or elected or appointed official of the city shall own any interest in any license or permit issued under this chapter; nor shall the family (as defined herein) of any city employee or elected or appointed official of the city who has any control over or who participates in official action or consideration of the license or permit or any involvement in the approval of any city alcoholic beverages licenses or permits in any way shall own any interest in any license or permit issued under this chapter; and
(6) The suitability of the premises for the conduct of an alcoholic beverage business, including its appearance, state of repair, maintenance standards, location, highway traffic problems, and the difficulty or absence thereof of policing by law enforcement agencies.
(e) The amount of initial license or permit and administrative fees shall be set initially and from time to time by resolution of the governing authority. Each application for a license or permit under this chapter shall be accompanied by a cashier's or certified check for the full amount of the initial license or permit fee, together with a separate check or cash for the administrative fees and other fees which are charged to defray investigative and administrative costs.
(1) If the applicant is denied a state license, the deposit representing the initial license fee shall be refunded, but the cost paid for the application, investigation and administrative costs shall be retained.
(2) Any applicant for a license or permit under this chapter who has an existing license under this chapter in existence at the time of making the new application shall pay an administrative fee of one-half the regular administrative fee, but shall pay a separate full initial license or permit fee for each license or permit.
(3) When an applicant is making applications for more than one license and/or permit at the same time, the applicant shall pay only one administrative fee of 150 percent of a normal administrative fee but shall pay a separate full license or permit fee for each license or permit.
(4) There shall be an annual license fee for each license and for those permits that are not temporary payable in advance for the entire year, beginning January 1 and ending December 31, of each year.
(5) Licenses shall expire on December 31 of each year and an application for renewal shall be made annually on or before the 31st day of October each year. Any licensee must annually meet the requirements set forth in this chapter in order to obtain a renewal of any license. Renewal applications received after October 31 shall incur a late fee of 20 percent of the renewal fee as a late charge penalty. This provision also applies to those permits that are not temporary.
(6) The payment of all license and permit fees in full shall be a prerequisite to the issuance of a license or permit unless otherwise provided by resolution of the governing authority.
(7) The imposition of a supervised action plan, suspension or revocation of any license or permit granted pursuant to this chapter shall not entitle the licensee or permit holder to a return of any portion of the license or permit fees.
(8) For new applications submitted after July 1, the license fee shall be reduced by one-half.
(f) As a prerequisite to the issuance of a license, the applicant shall furnish a complete set of fingerprints to be forwarded to the state bureau of investigation, which shall search the files of the state crime information center for any instance of criminal activity during the five years immediately preceding the date of the application. The state bureau of investigation shall also submit the fingerprints to the federal bureau of investigation under the rules established by the United States Department of Justice for processing and identification of records. The federal record, if any, shall be obtained and returned to the office submitting the fingerprints.
(g) All licensees/permit holders shall have a manager on the premises or at an event/location at all times when alcoholic beverages are manufactured, distributed, dispensed or sold.
(1) Any person or entity desiring to obtain an alcoholic beverage license or permit as enumerated in this chapter, shall file with the initial application an affidavit affirming that prior to any sales or services of alcoholic beverages, all employees, managers, cashiers, and servers, or future employees, managers, cashiers, and servers will be trained in the regulations governing the sale of alcoholic beverages prior to being allowed to sell or serve, and that a copy of the applicant's policies and procedures for such sales and services be attached to the affidavit, which policies and procedures the applicant shall prepare and promulgate to all employees, and which shall include adherence to this chapter.
(2) Upon a license or permit being granted, an affidavit signed by each employee, manager, server, cashier or other person handling the sale or service of alcoholic beverages in any way, including owners who work in any premises selling alcoholic beverages, attesting that the person has received the required training and certification through Rserving.com, is familiar with this chapter, and has read and agrees to follow the written policies and procedures provided to each such person. Proof of the employee's affidavit must be maintained by the employee and by the licensee. The City has a right to view said affidavit for inspection at any time.
(h) Any person or entity desiring to obtain an alcoholic beverage license as enumerated in this chapter, shall advertise the applicant's intention to make application to the city for the issuance of a license.
(1) Such advertisement shall be in such form as the governing authority may from time to time prescribe and shall be published for at least two consecutive weeks in the newspaper which shall be the legal organ of the county.
(2) Such advertisement shall contain a statement showing the location and name of the proposed business and the name of the applicant. The advertisement shall be at least one-eighth of a page and of at least an eight-point font size.
(3) The advertisement prescribed in this section shall not be required of applicants for licenses where the license sought is a renewal of a prior license issued to the same applicant for the same location.
(4) If the same location was previously licensed to do business, but there has been a change of ownership of the business or of other interest therein, the advertisement shall be required.
(5) If the location of a license changes, the advertisement shall be required, along with other requirements being met.
(6) When the advertisements have been published, the applicant shall obtain an affidavit of publication and shall attach the affidavit of publication to the written application for an alcoholic beverage license.
(i) A person or entity doing business at more than one establishment shall take out and pay for a separate license and/or permit for each place of business.
(j) No person, firm or corporation shall be granted any alcoholic beverage license or permit or shall serve as a registered agent (as defined herein) unless it shall appear to the satisfaction of the Mayor that such person, partners in the firm, officers and directors of the corporation have not been convicted or plead guilty or entered a plea of nolo contendere, and have been released from parole or probation, to any crime or ordinance violation involving moral turpitude; illegal gambling; illegal possession or sale of controlled substances or weapons; illegal possession or sale of alcoholic beverages, including the sale or transfer of alcoholic beverages to minors in a manner contrary to law; driving while under the influence of alcohol and/or drugs; obstruction or hindering of law enforcement officers; riot; inciting to riot; giving false information to law enforcement officer; and/or hindering apprehension or punishment of a criminal within a period of five years immediately prior to such application, keeping a place of prostitution, pandering, pimping, public indecency, prostitution, solicitation of sodomy, or any sexual related crime within a period of ten years immediately prior to the filing of such application.
(k) No license for the sale of alcoholic beverages shall be granted to any person convicted under any federal, state or local law of any felony, within ten years prior to the filing of application for such license. For purposes of this chapter, a conviction or plea of guilty or nolo contendere shall be ignored as to any offense for which defendant who was sentenced under the Georgia First Offender Act (O.C.G.A. tit. 42, ch. 8, art. 3, § 42-8-60 et seq.), except, however, that any such offense shall not be ignored where the defendant violated any term of probation imposed by the court granting first offender treatment or committed another crime and the sentencing court entered an adjudication of guilt as to the crime for which defendant had previously been sentenced as a first offender.
(l) At the time an application is submitted for any alcoholic beverage license or permit, the applicant shall, by a duly sworn affidavit, certify that the applicant, registered agent, and any owner(s) of the subject establishment meet the qualifications set forth in subsections (j) and (k) of this section 4-7.
(m) Any establishment holding a license or permit issued under this chapter shall at all times during the hours that the establishment is open to the public, be open to inspection by any law enforcement official, any officer of the sheriff's department or any license inspector of the county or to any person designated by the city council or the governing authority for purposes of compliance with this chapter.
(n) Alcoholic beverage licenses and permits issued under this chapter shall not be transferable or assignable to new owners, except as allowed in this section. Where there is a change in the ownership of a business, the new owner(s) shall file an application for a new license or permit within 30 days of the change in ownership and shall pay a new initial license or permit fee. In the event the new owner(s) timely file an application for a new license or permit, the original license or permit may be transferred to the new owners and shall remain in effect while the new application is being reviewed, but in no event shall this transfer period be longer than 30 days from the date of submission of the application by the new owner(s). Changes of business interests from one party at interest named in the original application to another party at interest named in the original application shall not be deemed a transfer of ownership; however, any such internal change of business interest shall be fully disclosed in writing to the city within ten days of the change in business interest.
(o) The application shall be in such form as shall be from time to time prescribed by the governing authority. The application form shall be obtained from the city clerk and submitted to the city clerk. It shall be signed by the applicant under oath, and shall be fully and completely executed. There shall also be attached to the application all required fees in full.
(p) When the verified, fully completed application, including the affidavit of publication, and payment of the license or permit fees and such other fees as may be required under this chapter are submitted to the city clerk, the city shall have up to 60 days to investigate the application and the background of the applicant.
(1) The city shall refer the application to the sheriff's department and the county building department for such investigations the city requires.
(2) The city shall cause an inquiry to be made into the city and county records to determine if the applicant, the registered agent, or other parties with an interest in an application for a license or permit under this chapter have any outstanding taxes or special assessments that are delinquent against his/her property or any other monies owing to the City and/or county. No license or permit shall be issued or renewed until such debts are paid in full.
(q) Upon completion of the investigation, the mayor may grant the applicable permit and/or the city council may grant the applicable license upon finding the following:
(1) The required fees have been paid.
(2) The application conforms in all respects to the provisions of this chapter and has been completely and fully executed, and each question on the form provided has been answered.
(3) The applicant has not knowingly made a material misrepresentation in this application.
(4) The applicant has fully cooperated in the investigation of the application.
(5) The applicant and registered agent meet the qualifications set forth in subsections (j) and (k) of this section 4-7 regarding criminal matters.
(6) The applicant has not had an alcoholic beverage license or other similar license or permit denied, suspended or revoked in any jurisdiction prior to the date of application.
(7) The building, structure, equipment, or location of such business, as proposed by applicant, complies with all applicable laws and provisions of this chapter.
(8) The applicant and the registered agent are each at least 21 years of age.
(9) If applicable, the residency requirement has been met.
(10) The applicant has not within five years of the date of the application committed or knowingly allowed or permitted any activity prohibited in this chapter in or upon the premises where such alcohol is to be located.
(11) That on the date the business for which a license is required in this chapter commences, and thereafter, there will be a responsible person of at least 21 years of age who meets all of the other requirements of this chapter on the premises to act as manager at all times during which the business is open.
(12) That the state distance requirements set forth in this chapter have been met.
(13) That the grant of a license will not state otherwise violate any local or state law.
(r) At the time and place that the license is to be considered by the city council, the applicant must appear in person and may be represented by an attorney at the meeting of city council. At the meeting, the city council shall vote for approval or denial of the applicant's license following deliberation in an open meeting. The vote shall occur as part of the agenda at a regularly scheduled city council meeting. The decision of the city council regarding the grant or denial of a license shall be final; any appeal may be made by certiorari to the superior court of the county.
(s) The mayor's decision to deny a permit is governed by those procedures set forth herein in subsection 4-33(b).
(t) Any material omission, or untrue or misleading information contained in or omitted from an original or renewal application for any license or permit issued under this chapter shall be unlawful, shall be just cause for a denial thereof, and shall be punishable as a violation of a city ordinance. If any such license or permit has previously been granted under the above circumstances, such material omission, or untrue or misleading information shall constitute cause for the revocation of such license or permit. Whenever there shall be a change in any of the facts reported to the city in the application for a license or permit under this chapter after such license or permit has been granted, it shall be the duty of the licensee or permit holder, within ten days after such change, to report the change to the city in writing.
(u) In addition to the provisions of this chapter, a licensee or permit holder is also charged with responsibility for strictly adhering to any other provisions of the City's Code, as well as the statutes and laws of the state and of the United States relating to the operation of the licensed or permitted business.
(v) Where a building or facility in which any person intends to operate under the provisions of this chapter is, at the time of the application for the license or permit, not in existence or not yet completed, a conditional license or permit may be issued for the location provided the plans for the proposed building show clearly a compliance with this chapter. No manufacturing, sales. or consumption shall be allowed in the establishment until the building or facility has been completed in accordance with the plans and is in conformity with all applicable city, county, and state laws.
(w) Any license or permit issued under this chapter shall automatically be null and void where the licensed or permitted business has not begun operation or has not operated or been open to the public for four consecutive months.
(x) All applicants for a license or permit (in the case of pending applications) and all licensees and permit holders (in the case of issued licenses and permits) shall forthwith report to the city any allegations of a violation of any state law or regulation or local ordinance or regulation when such allegations are made by the state department of revenue, a law enforcement officer, tax commissioner or prosecuting attorney in this state which charges the applicant or the licensee, as the case may be, with the violation of any law or regulation which could or would, in the event of a finding of guilt, result in an imposition of a supervised action plan, suspension or revocation of such license or permit or denial of an application for such license or permit. An applicant, a licensee, or permit holder shall report to the City all findings of such violation by any court, administrative agency, or tax commissioner which under this chapter could or would result in revocation or suspension of a license or permit or denial of an application. Failure to make reports required by this section shall itself be grounds for suspension or revocation of a license or permit or the denial of any application for a license or permit as the city council shall determine.
(y) An applicant, by filing an application for an alcoholic beverage license or permit, submits to all of the terms of this chapter and agrees to furnish such evidence, oral or written, as the city council shall find to be reasonably necessary to the determination of the application, and such applicant further agrees by the filing of such application that if a license or permit is issued thereon, to comply with the terms of this chapter.
(z) All licenses and permits issued under this chapter shall be subject to the Georgia Alcoholic Beverage Code, as now or hereafter amended, and those rules and regulations prescribed by the state department of revenue regarding alcoholic beverages. Violation of these statutes and/or regulations shall be violations of this chapter.
(aa) Any license or permit issued pursuant to this chapter shall be in such a form as shall be adopted by the city council.
