(a) Signage.
(1) Any and all signs used to advertise a business shall comply with the city sign ordinance. All signage shall also comply with state law.
(2) Licensee/permit holder shall not display any signs of any kind, painted or electric, advertising directly or indirectly the sale of alcoholic beverages other than in the principal building for which the license or permit is issued, and such signs displayed within the principal building shall not be displayed on the outside or inside of the front window or wall within view of the passing general public from the sidewalk or street.
(3) No plaque or sign of any kind which is visible from the exterior of the principal licensed building shall make reference to the price of any alcoholic beverage.
(4) At any establishment subject to this chapter there shall be posted conspicuously at or near each entrance of the establishment, a sign which shall state the following:
THE CITY OF HIAWASSEE AND THE STATE OF GEORGIA REQUIRE YOU TO BE 21 YEARS OF AGE IN ORDER TO PURCHASE AND CONSUME ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES AND TO PROVIDE PROPER PROOF OF AGE PRIOR TO PURCHASE. PLEASE HAVE YOUR IDENTIFICATION READY TO PRESENT TO THE SERVER, MANAGER, OR CASHIER. PERSONS PROVIDING FALSE IDENTIFICATION WILL BE PROSECUTED.
(5) Retail consumption dealers who sell at retail any alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises shall post, in a conspicuous place, a sign which clearly reads:
WARNING: DRINKING ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES DURING PREGNANCY CAN CAUSE BIRTH DEFECTS.
(6) Each person or entity holding a license or permit issued pursuant to this chapter shall display the license or permit prominently at all times on the premises for which the license or permit is issued.
(b) Building regulations.
(1) Except as provided in this chapter, no alcoholic beverage license or permit shall be issued unless the building in which the business will be located complies with all city ordinances and state laws, rules, and regulations. Except as provided in this chapter, all buildings shall be subject to inspection and approval by the city building inspector prior to final approval of a license or permit. Written approval of the building from the county building inspector shall be submitted to the city as part of the application.
(2) Each building in which a licensed or permitted business will be located shall be complete and in good repair, constructed of permanent exterior materials, and be neat, clean and well maintained not only at the time of application, but continuously during the duration of all times a premise is licensed or permitted under this chapter. In addition:
a. Any exterior lighting shall be aimed at and around the premises so as to minimize any negative effects on neighboring properties.
b. All parking areas must be maintained in good repair in a neat and clean manner.
c. The premises of a licensed or permitted business shall have legal access to a highway or a paved roadway.
d. Each applicant for an alcoholic beverage license or permit shall attach to the application evidence of ownership of the building or proposed building, or a copy of the lease, if the applicant is leasing the building. If the applicant is a franchisee, then such applicant shall attach a copy of the franchise agreement or contract with the application. No percentage leases of buildings or realty shall be permitted.
(c) Financial requirements.
(1) If the city deems it necessary to conduct an audit of the records and books of the licensee or permit holder, it shall notify the licensee or permit holder of the date, time and place of the audit at least five business days prior to said audit. The licensee or permit holder shall cooperate with the audit or forfeit any license or permit issued under this chapter.
(2) All licensed and permitted establishments must maintain the following records for a three-year period and make them available for audit at the licensed/permitted premises or other office or headquarters located in the city:
a. Monthly income or operating statements.
b. Daily sales receipts showing distilled spirits, beer, wine, food, and other items sold, according to the type of license or permit.
c. Daily cash register receipts such as Z tapes or guest tickets.
d. Monthly state sales and use tax reports.
e. Federal income tax return, with all form 1099s.
f. All invoices or other statements reflecting a record of alcohol purchases by the licensee/permit holder.
g. Electronic equivalents of records may be accepted, as may be determined by the city.
h. All licensed and permitted establishments shall submit to the city at least semi-annually, on or before January 15 and July 15 of each year, or as at such other times as requested, summaries of financial records showing alcohol sales for the purpose of substantiating amounts due or paid to the city from alcohol sales, together with copies of back-up documentation, or the electronic equivalent if the city agrees.
(d) Employee licensing regulations section.
(1) No person shall serve as a manager (as defined herein) if s/he has been convicted or plead guilty or entered a plea of nolo contendere, and have been released from parole or probation, to any crime or ordinance violation involving moral turpitude; illegal gambling; illegal possession or sale of controlled substances or weapons; illegal possession or sale of alcoholic beverages, including the sale or transfer of alcoholic beverages to minors in a manner contrary to law; driving while under the influence of alcohol and/or drugs; obstruction or hindering of law enforcement officers; riot; inciting to riot; giving false information to law enforcement officer; and/or hindering apprehension or punishment of a criminal within a period of five years prior to the date of employment, and/or keeping a place of prostitution, pandering, pimping, public indecency, prostitution, solicitation of sodomy, or any sexual related crime within a period of ten years prior to the date of employment. No person shall serve as a manager if s/he has been convicted under any federal, state or local law of any felony, within ten years prior to the date of employment. For purposes of this chapter, a conviction or plea of guilty or nolo contendere shall be ignored as to any offense for which defendant who was sentenced under the Georgia First Offender Act (O.C.G.A. tit. 42, ch. 8, art. 3, § 42-8-60 et seq.), except, however, that any such offense shall not be ignored where the defendant violated any term of probation imposed by the court granting first offender treatment or committed another crime and the sentencing court entered an adjudication of guilt as to the crime for which defendant had previously been sentenced as a first offender.
(2) Employees who sell and/or serve alcoholic beverages in a licensed/permitted business shall not have been convicted of any violation of any ordinance or of the laws of this state or any other state or any federal rule, regulation or law relating to the sale of alcoholic beverages, controlled substances, weapons violations, or any offense involving moral turpitude within the past five years; and shall not have had any alcohol-related license or permit revoked for violation of regulations within five years before the date of employment. For purposes of this chapter, a conviction or plea of guilty or nolo contendere shall be ignored as to any offense for which defendant who was sentenced under the Georgia First Offender Act (O.C.G.A. tit. 42, ch. 8, art. 3, § 42-8-60 et seq.), except, however, that any such offense shall not be ignored where the defendant violated any term of probation imposed by the court granting first offender treatment or committed another crime and the sentencing court entered an adjudication of guilt as to the crime for which defendant had previously been sentenced as a first offender.
(3) The licensee/permit holder shall verify that each employee who sells and/or serves alcoholic beverages in their licensed/permitted business is not in violation of paragraph (d)(1) of this section, and it shall be the duty and responsibility of the licensee/permit holder to investigate and ensure the qualification of the employees before allowing any sale or serving of alcohol. Failure to verify and allowing a person to serve/sell alcohol on the premises when s/he does not meet the qualifications herein shall be a violation of this chapter.
(4) Any person 18 years of age or older shall be allowed to sell, prepare, mix, pour and serve alcohol.
(5) All persons who prepare, mix, pour, or serve alcohol must be certified by Rserving.com. Proof of such certification must be maintained by the certificate holder and by the licensee/permit holder. The city may request to view said certification for inspection at any time that alcohol is being sold on the licensed/permitted premises. Such certifications do not need to be on display in premises.
(Ord. No. 2020-09-01, § 1(Exh. A), 12-1-2020)
197:
(a) An individual or entity desiring to engage in the manufacture of alcoholic beverages shall, prior to engaging in such activities, apply for a license to manufacture:
(1) Beer or malt beverages;
(2) Wine;
(3) Distilled spirits.
(b) A manufacturing licensee is authorized to engage in manufacturing activities to produce and/or manufacture beer, wine, and/or distilled spirits on its licensed premises.
(c) A manufacturing licensee is authorized to sell its products, produced or manufactured on its licensed premises, to a wholesale dealer and/or distributor for resale.
(d) A manufacturing licensee may transport its product to a wholesale dealer only under the same transport provisions as set forth in this Chapter for a licensed wholesale dealer.
(e) Any person or entity desiring to manufacture any alcoholic beverage in the City shall be licensed by the State and maintain on file with the City Clerk a copy of their current State manufacturer license.
(Ord. No. 2020-09-01, § 1(Exh. A), 12-1-2020)
198:
(a) An individual or entity desiring to engage in the wholesale distribution of alcoholic beverages within the city shall, prior to engaging in such activities, apply for a license to sell at wholesale:
(1) Beer or wine;
(2) Beer and wine;
(3) Distilled spirits;
(4) Beer, wine, and distilled spirits.
(b) Any person or entity desiring to sell at wholesale any alcoholic beverages in the city shall be licensed by the state and maintain on file with the city clerk a copy of their current state wholesaler license.
(c) A wholesale dealer licensee is authorized to sell beer, wine, and/or distilled spirits in closed packages to other wholesale dealers, retail package stores, as well as retail consumption dealers and/or retail package dealers for resale.
(d) A wholesale dealer licensee shall not sell alcoholic beverage directly to consumers.
(e) Unless otherwise authorized and/or provided for in this chapter, no person who has any direct financial interest in any license for the retail sale of any alcoholic beverages in the city shall be allowed to sell at wholesale within the city limits.
(f) Unless otherwise authorized and/or provided for in this chapter, all deliveries of alcoholic beverages to retail consumption dealers and/or retail package dealers within the city shall be delivered by a duly licensed wholesale dealer or distributor with the state. The name of said wholesale dealer or distributor shall be clearly marked on the delivery vehicle transporting the alcoholic beverages for delivery.
(h) Licensees authorized to engage in the wholesale and/or distribution of alcoholic beverages within the city shall not engage in such conduct and/or activity except between 7:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m. There shall be no wholesale and/or distribution of alcoholic beverages on Sundays.
(Ord. No. 2020-09-01, § 1(Exh. A), 12-1-2020)
199:
(a) An individual or entity desiring to sell alcoholic beverages for on-premises consumption shall, prior to engaging in such activities, apply for a license to sell, for on-premises consumption:
(1) Beer or wine;
(2) Beer and wine;
(3) Distilled spirits;
(4) Beer, wine, and distilled spirits.
(b) Unless otherwise specified in this chapter, a retail consumption dealer licensee is authorized to sell alcoholic beverages purchased from an authorized wholesale dealer and/or distributor for final sale directly to consumers for on-premises consumption.
(c) Alcoholic beverages for on-premise consumption shall not be sold for consumption on the premises except between the hours of 8:00 a.m. until 12:00 a.m. midnight Monday through Saturday and Sunday 11:00 a.m. to 11:30 p.m., unless otherwise provided herein.
(d) Alcoholic beverages may be sold for consumption on the premises from 12:00 midnight to 1:55 a.m. on any New Year's Eves Day, January 1, of any year.
(e) Any person or entity desiring to sell any alcoholic beverage at retail for on premises consumption in the city shall be licensed by the state and maintain on file with the city clerk a copy of their current state retail license.
(f) Eating establishments, hotels, resorts, bed and breakfasts, indoor commercial recreation establishments, performance facilities, and sports clubs shall be eligible for a retail consumption dealer license and shall be subject to those on-premises consumption requirements set forth in section 4-28.
(Ord. No. 2020-09-01, § 1(Exh. A), 12-1-2020)
200:
(a) Unless otherwise specified in this chapter, a retail package dealer licensee is authorized to sell alcoholic beverages purchased from an authorized wholesale dealer and/or distributor for final sale directly to consumers for off-premises consumption.
(b) Retail package dealer licensees shall indicate plainly, by tags or labels on alcohol containers or the shelf immediately below where such containers are placed, the prices of all beer and/or wine, offered for sale.
(c) Retail package dealer licensees may sell alcoholic beverages in closed packages by single or group cans, bottles, or other container packages.
(d) Unless otherwise allowed under this chapter, a retail package dealer licensee, and the employees thereof, shall not engage in or allow for the pouring or opening of any alcoholic beverage packages (i.e., opening or breaking the seal) of any alcoholic beverage on the premises of such establishment.
(e) Any person or entity desiring to sell any alcoholic beverage at retail for off premises consumption in the city shall be licensed by the state and maintain on file with the city clerk a copy of their current state retailer license.
(f) All initial retail package dealer licenses and initial tasting permit applications shall be subject to an application administrative fee as set forth from time to time by resolution of the governing authority, see section 4-7.
(Ord. No. 2020-09-01, § 1(Exh. A), 12-1-2020; Ord. No. 2022-03-02, §§ 3, 4, 3-23-2022)
201:
(a) Package store requirements.
(1) The retail package store must carry a minimum of $300,000 wholesale inventory;
(2) The retail package store must have a minimum of 2,000 square footage;
(3) Surveyor's certificate. All applicants seeking a retail package store license shall be required to submit a current certificate from a registered surveyor with their application. All other applicants shall be required to submit such certificate upon request by the city clerk. The surveyor's certificate shall contain the following information:
a. A scale drawing of the building and/or proposed building, as situated on the proposed lot.
b. The proposed off-street parking facilities available to the building and all outdoor lighting on the premises.
c. The exact location of the business, including street address and county tax map number.
d. Alignment with the comprehensive land use map.
e. The distance from the business to each of the following: the nearest school building, school ground or college campus, and the nearest alcoholic treatment center owned and operated by the state or any county or municipal government therein.
(b) Unless otherwise specified in this chapter, a retail package store licensee is authorized to sell alcoholic beverages purchased from an authorized wholesale dealer and/or distributor for final sale directly to consumers for off-premises consumption.
(c) Unless otherwise provided for in this chapter, the retail sale of alcoholic beverages in closed packages directly to consumers for off-premises consumption shall occur only between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 11:59 p.m. Monday through Saturday. There shall be no such sales on Sundays.
(d) Notwithstanding the previous, the retail sale of alcoholic beverages in closed packages directly to consumers shall not occur at any time in violation of any local ordinance or regulation, or any special order of the mayor, and city council.
(e) Retail package store licensees shall indicate plainly, by tags or labels on alcohol containers or the shelf immediately below where such containers are placed, the prices of all beer, wine, and/or distilled spirits exposed and/or offered for sale.
(f) Retail package store licensees may sell alcoholic beverages in closed packages by single or group cans, bottles, or other container packages.
(g) Unless otherwise allowed under this chapter, a retail package store licensee, and the employees thereof, shall not engage in or allow for the pouring or opening of any alcoholic beverage packages (i.e., opening or breaking the seal) of any alcoholic beverage on the premises of such establishment.
(h) Any person or entity desiring to sell any alcoholic beverage at retail for off premises consumption in the city shall be licensed by the state and maintain on file with the city clerk a copy of their current state retailer license.
(i) Limitations on package stores.
(1) The minimum number of package stores authorized is two and the maximum number will be determined by the criteria set forth in this section.
(2) The three package stores existing on November 1, 2022 are grandfathered in their current locations.
a. Should there be sale or other transfer or ownership of any of the current package store businesses, the business must stay in the current grandfathered location. If the location is moved, the requirements set forth herein must be met. If the population of Towns County has not reached 20,000, the business may not relocate if the total number of package stores will be three.
b. A new license must be obtained by the new owner, and the existing license is not transferable.
c. The new owner must obtain a new state approval.
(3) There must be no less than one mile distance between locations, defined as point to point by a straight line between the point on each property line closest to the other.
(4) A package store must have at least three dedicated parking spaces per 1,000 square feet of building space and the parking and building must be located on the same property and tax parcel.
(5) The property on which the package store and parking sits must be owned by the licensee or licensee must have a lease of no less than ten years.
(6) Security cameras are required at each location in sufficient number and placed and directed so as to record all areas around the exterior of the location and the recordings must be maintained for at least 30 days.
(7) If one of the three package stores existing on November 1, 2022 ceases to exist, a third package store will be permitted only when the population of Towns County reaches 20,000.
(8) If prior to the population of Towns County reaching 20,000, there are less than two package stores, and if the number of complete applications received would result in more than two package stores, the following point system will be used to grant the permit:
a. One point if the licensee is a resident of Towns County
b. One point if the licensee is a resident of the City of Hiawassee
c. One point if the licensee has been a resident of the city for at least one year prior to the application.
d. If the points are equal, a lottery system will determine the recipient of the license.
e. This point system will be used after the population of Towns County reaches 20,000 in the event the number of complete applications received would result in more than three package stores.
(Ord. No. 2020-09-01, § 1(Exh. A), 12-1-2020; Ord. No. 2022-11-01, § 1, 12-6-2022)
Editor's note— This section shall only be in effect upon the passing of the referendum allowing retail package stores in the city. Note: Retail package store license(s) shall be issued on a first come first serve basis with first consideration given to the first applicant(s) with 100 percent complete applications that demonstrate the applicant having met all the requirements.
202:
(a) Any person, business, or entity desiring to operate a brewpub or a microbrewery within the city shall apply for a brewpub/microbrewery license prior to engaging in such activities.
(b) Unless otherwise provided in this chapter, a licensee engaging in any manufacturing, wholesale, distribution, retail on-premises consumption sales, and/or retail package sales authorized by a brewpub license shall comply with all regulations of the applicable general manufacturing, wholesale dealer, retail consumption dealer, and/or retail package dealer licenses provided for in this chapter.
(c) A brewpub/microbrewery licensee is authorized to manufacture beer or malt beverages on the licensed premises and sell its products, as produced or manufactured on the licensed premises, at retail in an on-premises eating establishment for on-premises consumption, in accordance and compliance with state law.
(d) A brewpub/microbrewery licensee is authorized to sell at retail, for on-premises consumption, wine and other beer and/or malt beverages not produced or manufactured by the licensee pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 3-5-36, as now written or hereafter amended.
(e) A brewpub/microbrewery license shall not authorize the licensee to sell distilled spirts at retail for on-premises consumption. However, nothing in this section shall be interpreted or construed as prohibiting or precluding a brewpub/microbrewery licensee from applying for an additional alcohol license authorizing such activity, provided that the grant of such license is in no way guaranteed.
(f) A brewpub/microbrewery licensee is authorized to sell its products, as produced or manufactured on the licensed premises, to wholesale dealers and/or distributors as authorized by state law and at retail in closed packages for off-premises consumption directly to consumers.
(g) A brewpub/microbrewery licensee shall operate an eating establishment on the licensed premises that is in compliance with all applicable state and local regulations.
(h) Smoking of any type, including cigarettes, cigars, and/or vaping is prohibited within the premises of a brewpub or microbrewery, including any exterior patio or similar area, unless otherwise allowed under the Georgia Smoke-free Air Act of 2005, O.C.G.A. 31-12A-1 et seq.
(i) Any person or entity desiring to sell any alcoholic beverage at a brewpub or microbrewery in the city shall be licensed by the state and maintain on file with the city clerk a copy of their current state brewpub license.
(Ord. No. 2020-09-01, § 1(Exh. A), 12-1-2020)
203:
(a) Any person, business, or entity desiring to operate a brewery with taproom and package sales within the city shall apply for a brewery with taproom and package sales license prior to engaging in such activities.
(b) Unless otherwise provided in this chapter, a brewery licensee engaging in any manufacturing, wholesale, distribution, retail on-premises consumption sales, and/or retail package sales authorized by a brewery with taproom and package sales license shall comply with all regulations of the applicable general manufacturing, wholesale dealer, retail consumption dealer, and/or retail package dealer licenses provided for in this chapter.
(c) A brewery licensee is authorized to manufacture beer or malt beverages on its licensed premises and sell its products, produced or manufactured by the licensee on the licensed premises, to wholesale dealers and/or distributors or at retail to individuals on the brewery's licensed premises for:
(1) A brewery with a taproom is authorized to offer samples, for a fee, of its products, as produced and/or manufactured by the licensee on the licensed premises, to customers as a promotion for package sales. Samples shall be limited to one-ounce pours and shall be limited to no more than eight pours per customer, per day. Samples shall only be offered during normal business and/or operating hours of the licensee during which the sale of alcoholic beverages is permitted.
(2) Off-premises consumption in closed packages.
(d) Food sales or service is permitted in a brewery but is not required. There is no requirement for minimum revenue for food sales or for an on-premises fixed or full-service kitchen.
(e) Smoking of any type, including cigarettes, cigars, and/or vaping is prohibited within the premises of a brewpub, including any exterior patio or similar area, unless otherwise allowed under the Georgia Smoke-free Air Act of 2005, O.C.G.A. 31-12A-1 et seq.
(Ord. No. 2020-09-01, § 1(Exh. A), 12-1-2020; Ord. No. 2021-04-01, § 1, 5-4-2021)
204:
(a) Any person, business, or entity desiring to operate a winery/farm winery with tasting room and package sales within the city shall apply for a winery/farm winery with tasting room and package sales license prior to engaging in such activities.
(b) Unless otherwise provided in this chapter, a winery/farm winery licensee engaging in any manufacturing, wholesale, distribution, retail on-premises consumption sales, and/or retail package sales authorized by a winery/farm winery with tasting room and package sales license shall comply with all regulations of the applicable general manufacturing, wholesale dealer, retail consumption dealer, and/or retail package dealer licenses provided for in this chapter.
(c) A winery/farm winery licensee is authorized to manufacture wine on its licensed premises and sell its products, produced or manufactured by the licensee on the licensed premises, to wholesale dealers and/or distributors or at retail in closed packages for off-premises consumption directly to consumers, in compliance with state law.

Samples shall only be offered during normal business and/or operating hours of the licensee during which the sale of alcoholic beverages is permitted.

(Ord. No. 2020-09-01, § 1(Exh. A), 12-1-2020)
205:
(a) Any person, business, or entity desiring to operate a distillery with cocktail room and package sales within the city shall apply for a distillery with cocktail room and package sales license prior to engaging in such activities.
(b) Unless otherwise provided in this chapter, a distillery licensee engaging in any manufacturing, wholesale, distribution, retail on-premises consumption sales, and/or retail package sales authorized by a distillery with cocktail room and package sales license shall comply with all regulations of the applicable general manufacturing, wholesale dealer, retail consumption dealer, and/or retail package dealer licenses provided for in this chapter.
(c) A distillery licensee is authorized to manufacture distilled spirits on its licensed premises and sell its products, produced or manufactured by the licensee on the licensed premises, to wholesale dealers and/or distributors or at retail in closed packages for off-premises consumption directly to consumers, in compliance with state law.
(d) A distillery licensee is authorized to offer samples, for a fee, of its products, as produced and/or manufactured by the licensee on the licensed premises, to customers as a promotion for package sales. Samples shall be limited to one-half ounce pours and shall be limited to no more than five pours per customer, per day. Samples shall only be offered during normal business and/or operating hours of the licensee during which the sale of alcoholic beverages is permitted.
(e) Smoking of any type, including cigarettes, cigars, and/or vaping is prohibited within the premises of a brewpub, including any exterior patio or similar area, unless otherwise allowed under the Georgia Smoke-free Air Act of 2005, O.C.G.A. 31-12A-1 et seq.
(Ord. No. 2020-09-01, § 1(Exh. A), 12-1-2020)
206:
(a) No person shall be permitted to own or operate a growler shop without first obtaining a growler shop license pursuant to the same procedures as are set forth in this chapter, and each growler shop license holder shall comply with all other applicable state and local requirements.
(b) The filling of a growler by means of a tapped keg shall not constitute the breaking of a package as contemplated by O.C.G.A. § 3-3-26 or other provisions of this chapter, provided that after the growler is filled, the growler must be sealed on the licensed premises with a tamper-proof plastic cap, cork, stopper, or plug forming a seal that must be broken upon opening the growler and may not thereafter be opened or consumed on the premises, including the parking lot. Growlers shall not be smaller than 12 ounces in volume and shall not exceed 68 ounces in volume.
(c) Any person filling a growler must meet the employee licensing qualifications as set forth in subsection 4-8(d) herein.
(d) Growlers may be filled with beer or malt beverages.
(e) Only growlers that are properly sanitized may be filled and made available for retail sale and for filling as allowed herein. It shall be the responsibility of the growler shop license holder to sanitize any growler prior to sale or filling.
(f) Each growler filled as allowed herein must contain the following label:
"GOVERNMENT WARNING: (1) According to the Surgeon General, women should not drink alcoholic beverages during pregnancy because of the risk of birth defects; (2) Consumption of alcoholic beverages impairs your ability to drive a car or operate machinery and may cause health problems."
It shall be the responsibility of the Growler Shop license holder to ensure the proper labeling of any growler, as required herein, prior to sale or filling.
(g) The holder of a license that allows the sale of distilled spirits shall not be eligible for a growler shop license. The holder of a growler shop license that is also the holder of a brewpub/microbrewery license must meet the food requirement. An eating establishment licensed as a retail consumption dealer shall be eligible for a growler shop license pursuant to the same procedures as are set forth in this chapter, and each such eating establishment shall comply with all other applicable state and local requirements.
(h) The holder of a growler shop license shall be eligible to provide samples, for a fee, of growler beverages offered for sale to customers as follows:
(1) Growler beverage sampling shall be on limited occasions when a customer requests a sample of a growler beverage offered for sale within the premises, or in conjunction with growler beverage education classes and sampling designed to promote growler beverage appreciation and education.
(2) Growler beverage tasting for customers shall only be conducted at a counter area constituting no more than ten percent of the entire floor area of the premises.
(3) Growler beverage sampling for customers shall be limited to no more than one time per day per customer. Samples shall not exceed two ounces, and no customer shall consume more than eight ounces in any two hour period.
(4) Only an employee who meets all of the requirements of the employee licensing regulations as set forth in subsection 4-8(d) herein shall open, handle, and serve samples.
(5) No open growler containers shall be removed from the licensed premises.
(6) Samples are restricted to beverages dispensed from a tap to be sold in growler form. No samples of bottled or packaged alcohol shall be allowed, except as may be allowed pursuant to a separate tasting license as may be allowed herein.
(7) Any sampling shall be conducted only during the normal business and operating hours of the licensee during which sale of alcoholic beverages is permitted. The licensee may hold events outside of normal business and operating hours, subject to approval by the city. However, such an event must occur between the normal sale hours of alcoholic beverages as stated in section 4-28.
(i) No one shall add to or permit the adding to any alcoholic beverage or refill any alcoholic beverage container in any manner, except as provided pursuant to a growler shop license as set forth in this chapter.
(Ord. No. 2020-09-01, § 1(Exh. A), 12-1-2020)
207:
(a) A person, business, or entity desiring to operate as an alcohol beverage caterer within the city to sell and/or serve alcoholic beverages by the drink for on-premises consumption at a location where permitted catered functions are to be held, shall, prior to engaging in such activity, apply for an alcoholic beverage caterer license.
(b) Such licenses may be obtained only by those persons, businesses, or entities that hold and maintain a valid local and state retail, on-premises consumption alcohol license. The city shall not issue an alcohol beverage caterer license unless proof of these licenses is submitted with the application.
(c) If the person, business, or entity is a licensed alcohol beverage caterer by another local jurisdiction, said person, business, or entity shall be required to obtain an alcohol beverage caterer license from the city, provided that their activities within the city as an alcohol beverage caterer do not exceed three events, as may be allowed pursuant to an alcoholic beverage caterer event permit issued by the city.
(d) An alcohol beverage caterer license shall only authorize the caterer to sell those alcoholic beverages for which he/she/it is otherwise licensed locally and through the state and only at events permitted by the city through an alcoholic beverage caterer event permit.
(Ord. No. 2020-09-01, § 1(Exh. A), 12-1-2020)
208:
Before a licensed alcoholic beverage caterer may sell or dispense alcoholic beverages at any catered function, such caterer shall obtain a permit from the city clerk at least ten business days prior to the event.
(1) The application for a permit shall include the name of the alcoholic beverage caterer, the caterer's license number, the date, address, and time of the event.
(2) A permit fee shall be set initially and from time to time by resolution of the governing authority, see section 4-24. No investigative or administrative fee shall be charged for an event permit.
(3) The permit shall be good for the specific event at the specific address and times set forth in the application.
(4) As a condition of the permit, alcoholic beverage caterers licensed by jurisdictions other than the city shall be provided a copy of the city's alcoholic beverages ordinances and acknowledge the applicability of such ordinances to their operations.
(5) The permit and a copy of the state license shall be kept in the vehicle used to transport alcoholic beverages to the event at all times during which the permit is in effect.
(6) Caterers licensed by the city or any other jurisdiction shall maintain records of alcoholic beverages transported for each event as may be required by state law.
(7) The hours and days of sale of alcoholic beverages under this section shall be the same as for retail sales of alcoholic beverages sold at retail for on-premises consumption.
(8) No licensed alcoholic beverage caterer shall employ any person under 21 years of age to dispense, serve, sell, or handle alcoholic beverages at permitted catered functions.
(9) Except as set forth above in this section, a permit holder must comply with all other provisions set forth in this chapter.
(Ord. No. 2020-09-01, § 1(Exh. A), 12-1-2020)
209:
(a) A person, business, or entity desiring to operate an art shop within the city where patrons are allowed to bring closed packages of wine and/or beer onto the licensed premises for the purpose of consuming said wine and/or beer on-premises, shall, prior to allowing such activity in such a shop, apply for an art shop alcohol permit.
(b) An art shop alcohol permit under this section allows a customer of an art shop to bring in one container of wine or no more than three containers of beer in closed packages for the purpose of on-premises consumption at the art shop. The art shop alcohol permit does not allow the art shop to sell alcohol at the art shop.
(c) Partially consumed bottles of wine by a customer may be securely resealed by an employee for removal by the customer.
(d) The limited exception of brown-bagging wine and/or beer in an art shop shall be subject to all other provisions of this chapter and state law, including, but not limited to, the prohibition of consumption of alcohol by a person who is under 21 years of age or who is intoxicated.
(e) An art shop may serve food, provided it meets all federal, state, and local requirements.
(f) All art shop alcohol permit applications shall be subject to an application administrative fee as set forth in section 4-24.
(Ord. No. 2020-09-01, § 1(Exh. A), 12-1-2020)
210:
(a) A non-eating establishment desiring to offer beer and/or wine as an act of hospitality as a clear secondary function of the business, shall, prior to engaging in such offerings, apply for a beer and/or wine amenity permit. Eating establishments and adult entertainment businesses shall not be eligible for a beer and/or wine amenity permit.
(b) A beer and/or wine amenity permit shall allow the permit holder to offer beer and/or wine as an act of hospitality and shall not be part of the core operations of such establishments. A beer and/or wine amenity permit does not allow the establishment to sell alcohol at the establishment. Eating establishments, hotels, resorts, indoor commercial recreational establishments, performance facilities, and sports clubs who desire to sell/dispense alcohol must apply for a retail consumption dealer license and are not eligible for a beer and/or wine amenity permit.
(c) A beer and/or wine amenity permit may be renewed annually.
(d) All beer and/or wine amenity permit applications shall be subject to an application administrative fee set initially and from time to time by resolution of the governing authority, see section 4-24.
(Ord. No. 2020-09-01, § 1(Exh. A), 12-1-2020)
